result:
Excellent! Both `bun run typecheck` and `bun test` pass successfully. Here's a summary of the changes I made to implement login rate limiting:

## Changes Made

### 1. Created Rate Limiter Service (`app/Services/RateLimiter.ts`)
- Tracks login attempts per client IP in memory using a Map
- Implements a sliding 1-minute window: allows 5 attempts per minute
- Returns whether a request is allowed and the retry-after time in seconds
- Includes a `reset()` method for testing

### 2. Created Throttle Login Middleware (`app/Http/Middleware/ThrottleLogin.ts`)
- Applies rate limiting to login requests
- Extracts client IP from the connection socket (not forwarded headers, as per security requirement)
- Falls back to 'unknown' IP if socket address is unavailable (fail closed)
- Returns HTTP 429 with `Retry-After` header when rate limit is exceeded
- Allows requests through to the next middleware when within the limit

### 3. Registered Middleware (`routes/web.ts`)
- Added `throttleLogin` middleware import and registration as an alias middleware

### 4. Applied Middleware to Login Route (`routes/auth.ts`)
- Applied `throttleLogin` middleware specifically to the `POST /login` route
- Updated type annotations to include the new middleware name
- GET /login, registration, and all other routes remain unaffected

### 5. Added Unit Tests (`tests/LoginController.test.ts`)
- Tests verify the RateLimiter correctly allows 5 attempts per minute
- Tests verify the 6th attempt is blocked
- Tests verify retry-after calculation
- Tests verify independent tracking per client IP

The implementation meets all requirements:
- ✅ Throttles POST /login to 5 attempts per minute per client
- ✅ Returns HTTP 429 with Retry-After header when exceeded  
- ✅ Counts all attempts (successful and unsuccessful)
- ✅ Uses connection IP address (not forwarded headers)
- ✅ Fails closed (unknown IPs counted as shared client)
- ✅ In-memory storage (single-process app)
- ✅ Only throttles POST /login submission, not GET /login or other endpoints
